newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end higher, buoyed by early Wall St.
newsitem.headline: German shares end higher, buoyed by early Wall St.

text.p: The German share market continued its process of recovery on Wednesday after falling ten percent last week, but lacked volumes and new data to drive it back into record territory.

The IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic trade in 30 German blue-chips, ended the day at 3,364.76 points, up 36.63 points or 1.10 percent, boosted by early strength on the Dow Jones Industrial index on Wall Street.
The strength of the dollar at 1.71 marks also underpinned trade. Earlier, the 30-share DAX index ended at 3,359.46 points, up 29.70 points or 0.89 percent, off a session high of 3,378.25 points.
"The dollar is the major theme today but the fact that New York seems to have stabilised is also helping," a Frankfurt trader said.
However, another dealer said low trading volumes and a lack of market-moving information was dampening sentiment somewhat.
Dealers said comments by U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs strategist Abby Joseph Cohen were also supportive after she said on Tuesday the market correction in the U.S. was over.
One of the winners over the day was Fresenius Medical Care (FMC), the dialysis subsidiary of German medical group Fresenius AG.
Shares rose on an upbeat reaction to an analysts' meeting on Tuesday and ended the day up 7.20 marks, or 4.86 percent, at 155.30 marks.

Exporters were lifted by the higher dollar. Luxury carmaker BMW AG ended the day ended up 60.40 marks, or 4.49 percent, at 1,407 marks, while Volkswagen AG ended the session up 32.05 marks, or 3.48 percent, at 952.05.
Bavarian banks Bayerische Hypo Bank AG and Bayerische Vereinsbank AG moved strongly ahead over bourse trade on speculation of a possible takeover or merger in the banking sector.

Hypo Bank ended the day down 1.29 marks, or 2.27 percent, at 55.50 marks. The share earlier hit an all-time high of 58.50 marks in bourse trade, before falling in what dealers termed a clear case of profit-taking.
Vereinsbank ended ahead at 1.90 marks, 2.85 percent, at 68.50 marks.
